objective: Revise the interactive configuration-management prototype so approval means artifact clearance, production results determine the current production version, and the complete workflow is usable on desktop and H5 without backend or database changes.
users: workflow approvers reviewing and signing tasks
project managers reviewing current production versions and analytics

requirements.statement: Provide production-window, version-application, production-baseline, production-version and analytics views under one configuration-management entry.
acceptance: All five views are reachable after login
Switching views preserves module context and uses one mock fact model
requirements.source: User optimization item 1 and selected option 1
counterexample: Production baseline and current production version remain merged in one ambiguous view

requirements.statement: Separate version type from application characteristic.
acceptance: Version types are regular, urgent and emergency
Additional is a derived read-only characteristic and maps to additional workflow codes
counterexample: Additional regular appears as a user-selectable version type

requirements.statement: Show rich production-window eligibility and prevent invalid selection.
acceptance: Each option shows code, name, four minute-precision timestamps, status and disabled reason
Closed, pre-declaration and already-producing windows cannot receive non-emergency applications
Declaration start defaults to the first day of the current month at 00:00
counterexample: A closed window looks selectable
Window periods omit time-of-day

requirements.statement: Drive application fields and validation from the emergency choice and derived version type.
acceptance: Emergency hides window, derived version type and requirement number
Emergency requires a description and at least one test-report attachment
Non-emergency requires at least one requirement and derives regular or urgent from window dates
counterexample: Emergency remains selectable from the automatic type field
An emergency application submits without a test report

requirements.statement: Show the latest successful production version for every selected delivery unit.
acceptance: The form displays version, version type and production time from current production data
No successful history produces an explicit empty value
counterexample: The form shows the latest approved version as if it were deployed

requirements.statement: Present duplicate applications with a complete business snapshot and status-dependent user choices.
acceptance: The dialog includes all original business information except attachments
Draft, returned and withdrawn records allow cancel, edit or create
In-review records allow create and require withdrawal before old-record edit or cancel
Cleared records only allow creating an additional application
requirements.source: User optimization item 10 and confirmed conflict rules
counterexample: The system silently blocks all duplicates
The dialog exposes old attachments

requirements.statement: Treat workflow approval completion as artifact clearance only.
acceptance: Approved applications and their delivery units enter the selected window as cleared candidates
Approval alone does not update the current production version
Workflow code is selected from version type and additional characteristic
requirements.source: User optimization item 1 and explicit rename from pending confirmation to artifact clearance
counterexample: An approval event immediately marks the version as deployed

requirements.statement: Maintain actual production outcomes in a window-scoped production baseline.
acceptance: The view lists the latest cleared candidate per subsystem and delivery unit by approval completion time
Outcomes are artifact-cleared, succeeded, failed and not-produced
Outcome corrections require reason and retain before value, after value, operator and time
requirements.source: User optimization item 1 and correction confirmation
counterexample: The candidate is chosen by lexical version comparison
A production result changes without an audit reason

requirements.statement: Provide a cross-window current production-version projection derived only from successful production history.
acceptance: Each subsystem and delivery unit shows latest successful version, type, production date and source window
Reversing a success recalculates the previous valid successful version
requirements.source: User optimization item 2 and correction confirmation
counterexample: A failed or merely cleared version appears as the current production version

requirements.statement: Assign emergency applications to a production window at approval completion.
acceptance: Approval within a production window assigns that window
Otherwise the nearest future window is assigned and remains fixed
Draft can be saved but submission is blocked when no current or future window can receive it
requirements.source: User optimization item 8 and final no-window confirmation
counterexample: The user manually selects an emergency window
An emergency application is approved with no resolvable window

requirements.statement: Provide one responsive workflow review route for release approvals.
acceptance: The route is /workflow/review/:taskId with businessType and businessId
The current valid assignee can view details and approve, reject, return and confirm signature
The same route uses desktop and H5 layouts without changing business behavior
requirements.source: User optimization item 11 and approved platform integration design
counterexample: H5 uses a second route with different approval rules
A non-assignee can execute an action

requirements.statement: Provide consistent analytics with multi-dimensional drill-down.
acceptance: Metrics cover windows, subsystems, delivery units, requirements, applications, version types, clearance and production outcomes
Charts and drill-down rows reconcile with the same mock facts
requirements.source: User optimization item 12 and prior report requirements
counterexample: Analytics counts differ from the application or production-baseline views

requirements.statement: Keep prototype controls out of the normal business interface while preserving development-state testing.
acceptance: The duplicate current-project, mock and state toolbar is absent from the normal page
Development-only debug mode can still show loading, empty, failure, forbidden and reset states
counterexample: Normal users see a Mock state selector above the business page

requirements.statement: Keep revision 2 frontend-only, responsive, reversible and shaped for future formal APIs.
acceptance: No Java, Flyway or real platform-service implementation changes
Desktop and 375x812, 390x844 and 430x932 paths have no page-level horizontal overflow
Removing revision-2 frontend changes restores revision 1
requirements.source: Approved prototype boundary and RDDMP H5 contract
counterexample: The prototype writes database state
The H5 approval page requires horizontal page scrolling

invariants: One application belongs to one project and one physical subsystem and contains at least one delivery unit
A delivery unit has exactly one artifact type: image or binary
Artifact files are not uploaded to the configuration-management module
Approval completion means artifact clearance and never implies successful production
Only a valid successful production history record can drive the current production version
Latest window candidate is selected by approval completion time rather than version-string ordering
Emergency window assignment is fixed after approval completion
Workflow and signature identity are validated by the server in the formal implementation
Prototype operations never claim durable persistence
constraints: Vue 3, TypeScript, Vite, Element Plus, ECharts and existing dependencies only
No server, database, Flyway, real workflow, notification, attachment storage or external-system changes
Use fictional project, subsystem, delivery-unit, requirement, task and attachment metadata
Attachment limit is 20MB per file and 10 files per application
Version values are required and may not contain spaces; semantic ordering is out of scope
Acceptance viewports are 375x812, 390x844, 430x932 and 1280x800 or larger
Development remains on local rokey as requested
non_goals: Formal configuration-management backend and database schema
Real project-management, R&D-management, requirement-management or test-defect integration
Artifact repository or artifact binary upload
Independent mobile application or separate H5 route
External digital signature or certificate authority
Semantic version comparison and automatic production-result detection

selected_approach.name: Unified domain mock with two-level baseline projections and one responsive approval route
selected_approach.reason: It makes clearance, actual production and current production versions independently observable while preserving a direct path to formal APIs and avoiding duplicated Web/H5 rules.

alternatives.name: Add production flags to the old baseline view
alternatives.rejected_because: It continues to mix cleared candidates, window outcomes and current production state and cannot safely recalculate history.

alternatives.name: Separate Web and H5 approval routes
alternatives.rejected_because: It duplicates task permissions, state transitions and signature behavior and creates drift risk.

inside: release prototype domain types and session repository
outside: formal project, subsystem, delivery-unit and requirement providers

components.name: release-prototype-repository
components.responsibility: Own deterministic session facts and atomic mock commands

components.name: project-context-provider
components.responsibility: Expose the current fixed mock project through a replaceable contract

components.name: window-view
components.responsibility: Present four timestamps, eligibility, state and regular-application switch

components.name: application-view
components.responsibility: Present list, form, type derivation, latest production version and duplicate decisions

components.name: production-baseline-view
components.responsibility: Maintain window-scoped candidate production outcomes and audit

components.name: current-production-view
components.responsibility: Project latest valid successful production per subsystem and delivery unit

components.name: analytics-view
components.responsibility: Derive metrics, charts and drill-down from the same facts

components.name: workflow-review-page
components.responsibility: Render one task and shared actions using responsive desktop/H5 layouts

interfaces.name: WindowQuery
interfaces.contract: Return window timestamps, status, selectable and disabledReason within current project scope.

interfaces.name: ApplicationCommand
interfaces.contract: Save, submit, withdraw, cancel and resubmit with requestId and dataVersion.

interfaces.name: ConflictQuery
interfaces.contract: Return complete historical business snapshots excluding attachments and explicit allowed actions.

interfaces.name: WorkflowLifecycle
interfaces.contract: Deliver lifecycle events at least once; release consumes idempotently by eventId, application code and workflow round.

interfaces.name: ProductionLedgerCommand
interfaces.contract: Update outcome with reason, requestId and dataVersion and retain audit.

interfaces.name: CurrentProductionQuery
interfaces.contract: Return latest valid successful production metadata for delivery units.

transitions: verify a current or future window exists
update latest window candidates by approvedAt

data_flows.output: updated production baseline and current production version

error_handling.behavior: Show field-local errors and preserve all entered data.

error_handling.condition: No current or future window can receive an emergency application
error_handling.behavior: Allow draft save but block submit with a window-maintenance message.
error_handling.recovery: Create an eligible production window and resubmit.

error_handling.behavior: Show the historical business snapshot and only status-allowed decisions.
error_handling.recovery: Choose cancel, edit or create as permitted.

error_handling.behavior: Do not overwrite server state; preserve local changes and show the conflicting current state.
error_handling.recovery: Reload and explicitly reapply the change.

error_handling.behavior: Map rule code to the affected field or delivery unit.
Show forbidden state and remove write actions.
error_handling.recovery: Return to an authorized view or obtain access.

error_handling.condition: Task is already processed or expired with 410
error_handling.behavior: Render read-only detail and the current task result.
error_handling.recovery: Return to inbox or business detail.

error_handling.behavior: Disable pending controls and reuse the same idempotency key.
error_handling.recovery: Render the command's final returned state.

security: Use fictional data only in the prototype
Formal write actions require authentication, RBAC, project scope, entity authorization and audit
Formal workflow and signature actors come only from the authenticated server context
performance: Derive analytics from normalized mock facts without duplicate metric stores
Formal latest-production lookups must support batch queries
Dispose ECharts instances when views unmount
compatibility: Keep existing overdue workflow codes while displaying urgent-version terminology
Use one route and action contract for Web and H5
No page-level horizontal overflow at required desktop and mobile viewports
Support light and dark themes without new dependencies
operations: Keep normal business UI free of debug controls
Formal implementation monitors workflow event retries, emergency assignment failures, production corrections and projection recalculation

verification_strategy.signal: Five views, window eligibility, version naming and field linkage match the confirmed rules.
verification_strategy.method: Vue build plus desktop browser application paths.

verification_strategy.signal: Latest successful production metadata and complete duplicate snapshots are visible with correct actions.
verification_strategy.method: Deterministic mock scenarios and browser interaction.

verification_strategy.signal: Clearance, production outcome, rollback projection and emergency assignment remain consistent across views.
verification_strategy.method: Cross-view state assertions and browser regression paths.

verification_strategy.signal: A valid pending task is actionable and an expired task is read-only on desktop and H5.
Analytics reconcile, debug controls stay isolated and the diff remains frontend-only.
verification_strategy.method: Metric cross-check, debug-mode checks, governance scope audit, git diff check and browser console inspection.

assumptions.text: Current project, subsystem and delivery-unit providers can remain mocked for this prototype revision.
assumptions.basis: User explicitly deferred those platform integrations.
assumptions.falsifier: The prototype is required to enforce real project or entity permissions.

assumptions.text: The platform workflow will expose code-based startup, lifecycle events, inbox/done projection and internal signature as separately designed.
assumptions.falsifier: The platform contract is rejected or its stable workflow-code interface changes.

assumptions.text: Existing frontend dependencies can support responsive review and analytics without a new package.
assumptions.basis: Revision 1 already uses Element Plus and ECharts.
assumptions.falsifier: An approved interaction cannot be implemented with current dependencies.

decisions.decision: Use separate production-baseline and current-production views.
decisions.reason: Window outcomes and cross-window production truth have different ownership and lifecycles.

decisions.decision: Approval completion means artifact clearance only.
decisions.reason: Approved artifacts may still fail or not enter production.
decisions.source: User optimization item 1 and explicit terminology confirmation.

decisions.decision: Display urgent version while retaining overdue workflow codes.
decisions.reason: Business terminology changes without breaking established workflow mappings.

decisions.decision: Treat additional as a derived application characteristic.
decisions.reason: It affects workflow risk handling but is not a version category.

decisions.decision: Assign emergency applications to a window at approval completion and then freeze assignment.
decisions.reason: Emergency users should not manually choose a window, while production accounting still needs one.

decisions.decision: Let the user decide how to handle duplicate applications within status constraints.
decisions.reason: Duplicates need warning and traceability but should not impose one universal resolution.

decisions.decision: Use one responsive workflow-review route for Web and H5.
decisions.reason: Permissions, actions and task state remain consistent across layouts.
decisions.source: User optimization item 11 and confirmed recommendation.

decisions.decision: Remove prototype controls from normal UI and expose them only through a development entry.
decisions.reason: Business users do not need Mock or state controls.

risks.risk: Revision-1 convergence evidence may be mistaken for revision-2 completion.
risks.impact: Unimplemented behavior could be reported as delivered.
risks.mitigation: Mark revision-1 evidence as historical and create a new plan, execution and observation cycle for revision 2.

risks.risk: Duplicated stored baseline and analytics values can diverge.
risks.mitigation: Store normalized facts and derive candidates, current production and metrics.

risks.risk: Emergency assignment may race with window changes.
risks.impact: An approved application has no stable accounting window.
risks.mitigation: Check availability before submit and perform atomic server-side assignment at approval completion in the formal implementation.

risks.risk: The complete conflict snapshot is dense on H5.
risks.impact: Actions or critical history become unreadable.
risks.mitigation: Use summary cards, expandable sections and a bounded scrolling dialog while excluding attachments.

approval.evidence: User confirmed the final architecture and interface section, then explicitly deferred the project-lifecycle expansion and instructed completion of the currently designed revision-2 scope.
